findings.claim: The legacy_counts and projects_of perl readers compare each frontmatter line to the exact string "---". chomp strips only \n, so a page with CRLF line endings fails the first-line test. Such a page is skipped silently. Its project is missing from the discovered list, and its legacy keys are missing from the vault-wide count. The script says a zero count means the vault is ready for retirement of the legacy keys, so this can produce a false zero. The readers also glob only wiki/memory/*.md, not subdirectories. Whether the migration command handles CRLF or subdirectories differently is not visible in the diff.

slug maps every character outside A-Za-z0-9._- to '_', so distinct project names such as 'a b' and 'a_b' share the same scratch files (sync-before-$s.txt, apply-$s.txt and so on). The later project overwrites the earlier one's results and the before/after comparisons mix them. The global `project` variable, set by the loops and read implicitly by lm, also makes the control flow hard to follow.

evidence: Only scripts/rehearse-card-page-migration.sh changed, and the whole diff was read.
The perl readers rely on the exact line '---' and on a non-recursive glob.
The per-project artifact file names are derived through the lossy slug function.
The live-path guard, the sqlite3 .backup copies and the HOME/XDG redirection are consistent with the commit's claims.
